slides.texte_overlay:
unusual hobbies that
make you a genius
Solving cryptic crosswords. Every clue is a small puzzle of language and logic. They train lateral thinking like nothing else. Start with an easy one on Sunday.
Learning to juggle. It sounds silly, but coordinating both hands trains focus and patience, and it's a great way to clear your head.
Mapping your family history. Old photos, records, questions to grandparents. You learn history, research and patience all at once.
Learning calligraphy. Slow, precise, calm. It trains your attention to detail and your patience, and the results look beautiful. Ten minutes a day is enough.
Collecting strange facts. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and my notebook of fascinating facts keeps growing. Free, quiet and calming.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. My notebook of fascinating facts keeps growing.

slides.texte_overlay: Building and flying model planes. Physics, patience and precision in one hobby. You understand how flight works by doing it. A fun weekend project.
Learning sign language. A completely new way of thinking about language, and a skill that can genuinely help someone one day. Start with the alphabet.
